💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that back in October 2017, I took off my Casio G-Shock for the last time, strapped on an Apple Watch Series 3, and haven’t looked back.
  • Also: I tested the Apple Watch Ultra 4, and these 4 upgrades matter most.
  • Given how attached I’ve become to the Apple Watch, it’s rare for me to even review any alternatives (I gave the Garmin Fenix 8 Pro a go, but it wasn’t for me), so I was surprised to find how much I liked the sub-$300 Mibro GS Explorer S Titanium, a watch from a lesser-known brand.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that back in October 2017, I took off my Casio G-Shock for the last time, strapped on an Apple Watch Series 3, and haven’t looked back. I worked my way up through Apple’s lineup until the Ultra was released in 2022. Today, I’m wearing an Ultra 4.

Also: I tested the Apple Watch Ultra 4, and these 4 upgrades matter most.

Given how attached I’ve become to the Apple Watch, it’s rare for me to even review any alternatives (I gave the Garmin Fenix 8 Pro a go, but it wasn’t for me), so I was surprised to find how much I liked the sub-$300 Mibro GS Explorer S Titanium, a watch from a lesser-known brand.

Industry observers note that I got to test the titanium version of the GS Explorer S, but note there’s a cheaper ceramic model that’s virtually identical except for three things — the material (titanium alloy vs. ceramic and fiber-reinforced polymer), mapping (only the titanium version has offline mapping), and of course, price.

According to recent reports, the weight is also slightly different at 0.18 oz, but that’s small enough to ignore. To keep things simple, I’m not including the titanium version with the metal band in this comparison.

Another feature that’s key to the success of a smartwatch is battery life.

Sources indicate that A few things stand out to me with this watch, both positive and negative. As an Apple Watch wearer, getting a couple of days from my Ultra is good, so I find going well over a week between charges quite remarkable. It eliminates that nightly charge, which I’d appreciate on those multi-day hikes where I’d normally take my Apple Watch charger.

Also: Suunto Race 3S review: How real-time dynamic pacing improved my trail runs.

Recent findings suggest that however, I’m so used to charging my Apple Watch nightly that it’s become a ritual, and switching to a weekly (or even less frequent) charging schedule makes it more likely I’ll forget. Also, it comes with a proprietary magnetic charging cable rather than a standard USB-C, which is a little more limiting. I suppose the good news is that if I lose it, there are replacements available.

I like that it comes with two bands, which gives more options. I’m a fan of orange, so that’s my choice there. And, in contrast to a lot of smartwatches, changing the band is relatively easy because it uses a custom quick-release spring bar that can be opened with a finger. Nice touch.

The Corning Gorilla Glass 3 gets a thumbs-up from me, despite being over a decade old. There are much worse materials to make a smartwatch crystal from, and I expect it to resist scratches, scrapes, and bumps well. For a rugged watch, the screen is the part most likely to get scratched, and decent protection is vital if the watch is to survive for any length of time.

In a recent development, however, it’s not invulnerable by any stretch of the imagination. And I know from experience that it won’t be anywhere near as durable as the sapphire that’s on my Apple Watch Ultra. But that’s in a totally different price category.

According to recent reports, another thumbs-up from me is the display’s 1,500-nit brightness, making it ideal for outdoor conditions. If you’re thinking of going for the titanium model to get your hands on mapping, know that the maps are limited to 31 x 31-mile (50 x 50 km) tiles, which explains the odd number. Also, while you get features such as route following, deviation alerts, one-tap return, and track-back navigation, it lacks advanced routing features like route creation and rerouting.

Also: I tried a $200 smartwatch with voice recording – it beat the Apple Watch in a few key ways.

The mapping is also somewhat sparse. But remember, I’m from the UK and we have excellent Ordnance Survey mapping of the entire country down to 1:25,000 resolution at an incredible level of detail. So for me, anything that doesn’t show me everything from big boulders on my path feels sparse.

Compare the mapping to what I can get on my Apple Watch from the mapping service in the Outdooractive app (iOS/Android).

Recent findings suggest that the Mibro Fit app is somewhat hit-and-miss, but it’s nowhere near as bad as the reviews made it out to be, so I feel it’s improved over the last couple of years. Yes, it’s a bit clunky and rough around the edges, but it did the job.

There’s no point bothering with an outdoor smartwatch if the data you’re gathering is inaccurate or incomplete. When reviewing outdoor gadgets, conscious of — and clear about — the fact that I’m one person, and the best I can do is compare one device against another. So, when I was testing the accuracy of the heart rate, SpO2, and location data, I compared them to the Apple Watch Ultra 4.

I tested the sensors while resting, walking, and hiking, and compared the data between the two devices. Two conclusions came from my testing:.

This is an obvious question that a lot of people are going to be asking, but it comes down to this: the Apple Watch is the clear winner, with one significant, glaring caveat. From the apps to advanced health features, optional 5G, and built-in payment handling, not to mention safety features such as fall and crash detection, the Apple Watch is better… if you have an iPhone.

Also: I tested the world’s first solar AMOLED sports watch – how charging works.

If you have an Android, the GS Explorer S is the better smartwatch. Compare this to, say, the Apple Watch SE 3, and you get better battery life (18 hours of normal use vs. 20 days), better GPS (single-band vs. dual-band), and better water resistance (164 feet vs. 328 feet, and the GS Explorer S is OK with diving to 98 feet). And if we’re comparing the titanium model, there’s mapping (although there are also plenty of mapping apps for the Apple Watch).

It leaves the SE 3 in the dust. I could compare it to the Ultra 4 and say you get a lot of outdoor smartwatch for a lot less, but it’s hard to make a fair comparison either way, given the major price difference and how mature the Apple Watch ecosystem is.

If you’re an Android user, the Apple Watch ecosystem isn’t on your radar, so the field is more open since flagships like the Pixel Watch 5 or Samsung Galaxy Watch 9 lean more toward being smartwatches than rugged outdoor watches (the exception being the Galaxy Watch Ultra).

Industry observers note that wearables have to fit into people’s style and aesthetic, and what I like might not suit you, so I like to offer some options. Here are a few alternatives you might want to check out:.

It has been revealed that watches are tough to review because they are so personal. I like major watches, but you might like small ones. I like a lot of information on the display, while you might like the bare minimum. We’re all different.

What I can say about the Mibro GS Explorer S is that, for the price (which at the time of writing is $140 and $230 for the ceramic or titanium models, respectively), it’s a very good outdoor smartwatch.

According to recent reports, also: Flipper Zero vs. Flipper One: Why the new model isn’t an upgrade.

If this does interest you, give thought to whether you want the ceramic or titanium version. The key difference is mapping, but I’m not fully sold on it because the map tiles are somewhat small and the routing features are limited when you’re actually on a route. Knowing this might tip you toward the ceramic model, unless you like the titanium look.

If you’re a fitness enthusiast, the GS Explorer S will give you all the stats you need to keep you on track, and more, for a very good price, and a device that should give you a good few years of service.

CVE-2024-10441 Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM) Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output VulnerabilityCVE-2026-40217 BerriAI LiteLLM Unprotected Alternate Channel VulnerabilityCVE-2026-90436 Apache Axis Unsafe Reflection VulnerabilityCVE-2026-90817 Vanderbilt University Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) Code Injection VulnerabilityThese types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities. CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria. Aware of an exploited vulnerability not at the moment listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form. Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance. Breaking: Traumatized teens sue school, cops after Doritos bag triggers AI gun alert

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1717 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, in October 2025, four Black high school students were sharing Cool Ranch Doritos after football practice, winding down and waiting for their rides home.
  • According to recent reports, within two minutes, Baltimore County Public Schools officials who reviewed security camera footage linked to the alert determined there was no actual threat.
  • The false alert could have ended there—before a traumatizing campus clash with police—but it didn’t.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, in October 2025, four Black high school students were sharing Cool Ranch Doritos after football practice, winding down and waiting for their rides home. It was then, in the lull of a moment any teen with after-school activities knows well, that the school’s AI gun detection system suddenly flagged one teen holding a bag of chips as a potential gunman.

According to recent reports, within two minutes, Baltimore County Public Schools officials who reviewed security camera footage linked to the alert determined there was no actual threat. They recognized the Doritos bag and canceled the alert, which notified not only other school officials but also the Baltimore County Police Department that no response was needed.

The false alert could have ended there—before a traumatizing campus clash with police—but it didn’t.

According to a lawsuit filed by the current and former students, Taki Allen, Yui-Osa Ogbeide, Devon Thompson Jr., and Keith Winfield III, due to “both technological and human errors,” school officials called police to the scene anyway, and the cops responded with force.

At least six patrol cars arrived with lights flashing, and some cops emerged with guns drawn. The teens froze and cooperated, confused and scared for their lives, their lawsuit remarked.

It has been revealed that “No one told the students what they were suspected of,” the lawsuit stated. “Officers separated the students, ordered them to their knees on the concrete, handcuffed them, and searched their persons and property.”.

It has been revealed that only after the cops failed to find a gun did students learn that it was the school’s AI gun detection system, Omnilert, that triggered the police response. Allegedly, one of the responding officers muttered, “stupid AI cameras” and “fucking Omnilerts,” while another told the students that “AI is not the best.” Finally releasing the students, one officer seemed to acknowledge that they had put the teens in danger.

According to recent reports, “Hey, thanks for not running away, that would have been a real problem,” the officer allegedly stated. Walking away, another joked that the boys should remember to “be careful with your chip bags.”.

The cops did not just target the suspected gunman but apparently told the other teens that they were guilty “by association” when they asked why they were searched.

Suing to stop any other teens from facing allegedly life-or-death situations due to officials’ blind trust of AI, the teens have asked for an injunction barring BCPS from using Omnilert until they can effectively establish protocols to prevent police responses to false alerts.

The lawsuit alleged that students’ constitutional rights were violated, as students were unlawfully searched and detained.

Damon Hewitt, president and executive director of the Lawyers’ Committee for Civil Rights Under Law—a nonpartisan nonprofit that’s representing the teens in the suit—stated that “overreliance on artificial intelligence technology mixed with inept communication and coordination among key officials is a toxic mix.”.

The complaint noted that BCPS was among the earliest adopters of Omnilert, and officials have touted it as “the largest deployment of AI visual gun detection” as a means to supposedly protect students. Instead, they alleged that Omnilert is marketing a defective product as triggering “near-zero false positives” without effectively requiring the adequate human review that claim depends on.

It has been revealed that “We need a reckoning on how AI is being used, especially concerning public safety and kids,” Hewitt said. “We are fighting to deliver justice in this case, but it also holds lessons for educators and police officials across the country who should think twice before putting our children’s fate in the hands of AI.”.

All the teens feel less safe on campus and less trusting of police following the incident. They also suffered from physical pain—including ”deep red marks” on their wrists from handcuffs—as well as “acute and lasting emotional distress, fear, anxiety,” and “humiliation.” Further, the teens report that rumors follow them around, falsely claiming that there was a gun and damaging their reputations.

Car pick-up will never be the same. The student falsely flagged as the gunman, Taki Allen, “no longer feels safe waiting for rides or spending time outside the school after hours” and “frequently pays for rides home from private car services to avoid waiting for rides from friends or family.” Keith Winfield’s house was very close to the school, but his mother, Frieda Winfield, said his anxiety was so bad that he would call her “multiple times after football practice ended to confirm that she was on her way to pick him up.”.

Frieda Winfield called for change following her son Keith’s chilling interaction.

“The police told my son this could have been a real problem,” Frieda Winfield mentioned. “No child in Baltimore County should face this kind of danger while waiting outside his own school for a ride home from his mother.”.

The teens’ lawsuit targets Omnilert and responding Baltimore County Police Department officers. It also challenges Baltimore County Public Schools and individual school officials who allegedly failed to establish proper protocols to prevent a police response to a canceled alert.

In a later investigation, the Office of the Inspector General (OIG) for Education concluded that Omnilert’s system had no “bias.” But OIG acknowledged that the “delegation of authority” process that Kenwood High School set up didn’t stop its principal, Kate Smith, from noticing the alert, failing to see it was canceled, and texting a school resource officer to deploy police 15 minutes later—all while acknowledging in that text that the object in the alert was “maybe not” a gun. Smith apparently was never trained on the Omnilert system, OIG’s report indicated.

The OIG agreed with teens that things should change. Immediately after the incident, an internal Omnilert training link was shared with BCPS staff, and OIG recommended that schools conduct biannual trainings moving forward.

Recent findings suggest that they also recommended that the BCPS Department of School Safety “review its protocol” and reduce the number of individuals who receive campus gun alerts. That could help ensure “internal notification controls are followed” and police “are fully informed of a verified threat,” the OIG said.

Without changes, the OIG acknowledged that “the loss of alert notification controls could place not only BCPS staff and students at risk but could also place responding law enforcement in a potentially tragic situation.”.

Industry observers note that another change offered a technical solution that may have prevented the tragic event. The OIG recommended that school officials switch to using the Omnilert app. Since Smith opened the alert in a text message window on her phone, they suggested that she could easily have overlooked the cancellation text message if her first instinct were to enlarge the image or review the camera footage.

Recent findings suggest that these recommendations aren’t enough for current and former students suing, one of whom remains an active student who claims the principal never apologized and instead made light of the incidents using cry-laughing emojis in texts with other school officials. Teens alleged that Smith should have known that more than “99 percent of OGD Alerts in Baltimore County Public Schools were false positives that required no police response,” as the OIG’s report stated, and she should have prioritized students’ safety and verified the threat before calling in police.

“BCPS’s failures amounted to deliberate indifference to the constitutional rights of its students,” their lawsuit alleged.

According to recent reports, the teens asked a court for an injunction barring the use of Omnilert until BCPS staff and police are adequately trained. In their complaint, they alleged that none of the officers on the scene had reviewed the camera footage before responding, and none of the officers informed of the alert cancellation intervened.

BCPS declined to comment on the lawsuit, pointing Ars to a statement issued to parents following the incident. That statement did not directly apologize to students but did say the school would provide “ongoing counseling and emotional support” to them while promising to take steps to prevent future incidents.

Blake Mitchell, Omnilert’s vice president of marketing, told Ars that Omnilert is reviewing the complaint.

According to recent reports, “What these four students went through on October 20, 2025 should not have happened, and we are truly sorry for the fear they and their families experienced,” Mitchell stated. “We understand why they want answers.”.

Mitchell said that Omnilert is “built to send anything that could be a firearm to trained people for review, because missing a real gun is the worst possible outcome.” He also reiterated that the OIG investigation found no bias in Omnilert’s system and seemed to agree that it was the school’s authority delegation that failed the students, not necessarily the technology.

Recent findings suggest that “In this case, the school’s designated safety staff reviewed the alert and canceled it within about two minutes, and everyone who received it was notified,” Mitchell remarked. “That is exactly why human review matters, and why a canceled alert must stay canceled.”.

Len Kamdang of the Lawyers’ Committee representing the teens told The Fresh York Times that teens want BCPS and Omnilert to acknowledge that “what happened to them was unacceptable.”.

“This case is ultimately about how human beings allowed AI to substitute for their judgment,” Kamdang said.

As a mother, Frieda Winfield told a local news outlet that she was shocked by the incident, despite deliberately teaching her son to be cautious around police. The boys’ caution “saved their lives in my opinion,” she said.

“I was angry. I was fearful,” Frieda Winfield said. “The biggest part was fear, because they’re young men. Young Black men, and they were at school, and they didn’t understand why what was happening, happened to them.”.

In a recent development, kamdang told NYT that “for anyone with children, that is a scary, scary situation. For a Black student, especially a young Black man in America, that is a life-or-death situation.”.

In a recent development, as AI tools are increasingly positioned as public safety solutions, the Lawyers Committee is pushing for police reform when cops or officials appear to be blindly trusting AI, their press release noted. They noted that “this injustice also raises a broader concern regarding the use and reliability of AI-powered technology in public safety where accuracy is essential in life-and-death situations.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that you don’t need to buy a gaming headset to play GTA VI on your PS5 or Xbox Series X|S.
  • In a recent development, it’s been a long 13-year wait for GTA VI, but with the holiday gift-buying season so close, you may be strapped for cash to buy a gaming headset, especially after spending $80 to $100 on the game.
  • According to recent reports, however, since your consumer headphones aren’t primed for console gaming, you’ll need to tweak some audio settings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that you don’t need to buy a gaming headset to play GTA VI on your PS5 or Xbox Series X|S. You can use headphones you already own by connecting them to your controller with a compatible audio cable and adjusting a few settings.

In a recent development, it’s been a long 13-year wait for GTA VI, but with the holiday gift-buying season so close, you may be strapped for cash to buy a gaming headset, especially after spending $80 to $100 on the game. The good thing is that GTA VI is strictly single-player right now, so you don’t need a headset with a mic to enjoy it. You can also easily turn a pair of headphones you already have into a makeshift gaming headset.

Also: Can your PC run GTA VI? Minimum requirements to expect.

According to recent reports, however, since your consumer headphones aren’t primed for console gaming, you’ll need to tweak some audio settings. Here’s what you need to know.

Whether playing on a PS5 or an Xbox Series X|S, you’ll need to wire your headphones to your controller. Neither console supports standard Bluetooth audio.

Your everyday consumer headphones have a different sound profile than gaming headphones.

Gaming headphones tend to offer clearer directional cues, so you can hear an enemy’s footsteps approaching. Consumer headphones are generally more bass-heavy, which can mask more intricate sounds of faraway dialogue, footsteps, or ambient sounds.

With a bass-boosted EQ, the low end of explosions, gunshots, and crashes may be too intense, and less prominent highs could make it harder to hear important cues like car doors full of a vengeful gang shutting, an NPC asking for a favor in the distance, or a scorned Leonidan whispering your location.

Also: Fake GTA 6 PC downloads are flooding the web.

According to recent reports, if you’re adamant about going wireless with your everyday headphones, you might try to use a Bluetooth dongle or a workaround with your TV. If you must use a dongle, it should support the same codecs as your headphones. If there’s a mismatch, the devices may default to the lower-quality SBC codec, potentially delivering poorer sound and higher latency.

If you connect your console to your TV and wirelessly connect your headphones to your TV, you may get a significant lag between your in-game actions and the audio in your headphones. I don’t recommend this either.

Also: How to play retro console games on modern systems: 3 ways.

According to recent reports, I also don’t recommend using high-impedance studio headphones, as your controller may not have enough power to drive them adequately. Finally, I don’t recommend using your headphones’ built-in spatial audio rendering at all, especially when it’s on top of your console’s rendering. Double spatial audio rendering can make your audio sound strange, and you may lose the directional cues spatial audio is supposed to enhance.

If you want spatial audio, configure these settings in your console’s audio settings.

According to recent reports, using your everyday headphones with your gaming console isn’t a long-term solution, but it can work in a pinch, especially if you want to play late into the night without disturbing your housemates. With some tweaking to your headphones’ and console’s audio settings, you can make it work, but before GTA VI Online comes out, put a solid pair of gaming headphones on your holiday wish list.

Sources indicate that google is retiring Google Assistant from smart speakers and displays in favor of Gemini for Home. The full switch is happening in Aug. 2027, when Google Assistant will be removed from these devices and replaced with Gemini.

In a recent development, google Home consumers have been able to opt in to use Gemini for Home since its rollout on smart speakers and displays like the Nest Audio, Nest Mini, and Nest Hub Max. Those who haven’t opted in will no longer be able to keep Google Assistant after Aug. 2, 2027.

Also: Google Wallet comes to your iPhone – but without this feature.

Powered by generative AI, Gemini for Home understands more natural phrasing than the rigid commands necessary to speak to Google Assistant.

Best early Black Friday MacBook deals: 8 I’d recommend shopping now

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s been a busy year for Macs, with the MacBook Neo and the fresh OLED touchscreen MacBook Pro.
  • Sources indicate that we’re watching deals on the new M5 MacBooks released just earlier in 2026 for price drops worth mentioning, from the thin and light MacBook Air models to the powerful MacBook Pro — the industry standard when it comes to performance and battery life.
  • Apple’s new MacBook Neo is a “near-perfect budget laptop,” according to ZDNET laptop reviewer Kyle Kucharski.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s been a busy year for Macs, with the MacBook Neo and the fresh OLED touchscreen MacBook Pro. To make room for all the new devices, this year’s MacBooks are already significantly discounted for the Black Friday/Cyber Monday sale period, which officially starts later this week.

Also: Best early Black Friday deals.

Sources indicate that we’re watching deals on the new M5 MacBooks released just earlier in 2026 for price drops worth mentioning, from the thin and light MacBook Air models to the powerful MacBook Pro — the industry standard when it comes to performance and battery life. We’re also seeing the first MacBook Neo deal since Apple’s price hike over the summer.

Also: Best early Black Friday Apple deals.

Apple’s new MacBook Neo is a “near-perfect budget laptop,” according to ZDNET laptop reviewer Kyle Kucharski. It’s designed for everyday tasks, internet browsing, media, and iPhone integrations, and it’s a snappy, battery-efficient laptop for those purposes. If you need more power though, you might want to look to the Air or the Pro models below. This is the first discount we’ve seen since Apple raised the price on this version from $699.00 to $799.00 in July.

Industry observers note that the 15-inch M5 MacBook Air is the larger of the two Air models, but still thin and lightweight — just 3.3 pounds. We gave the 15-inch our Editors’ Choice award for its fantastic battery life, lovely display, and how Pro it feels, with the 10-core M5 chip and 153Gb/s memory bandwidth.

Also: ZDNET’s Gift of the Year awards.

In a recent development, the latest and greatest in Apple’s thin-and-light MacBook lineup is currently $100 off — a solid discount for a laptop that just came out this spring. The M5 MacBook Air comes with more memory standard (16GB) and 512GB of local storage. It also supports Touch ID, Wi-Fi 7, and the 13-inch model weighs just 2.7 pounds, easily slipping into a bag unnoticed.

The base model MacBook Pro M5 is still the best option for consumers who want the processing power of the Pro line, but don’t need to spend the cash on higher-end models, which can run several thousand dollars. This model features 16GB of unified memory, a gorgeous Liquid Retina XDR display at up to 1600 nits peak brightness, faster processing power with the 10-core CPU, and of course, up to 24 hours of battery life.

Also: I compared the M5 MacBook Pro to older Mac models – here’s my buying advice.

In a recent development, for users looking for all the power of the M5 Pro, the model with 24GB of memory and 2TB of local storage is almost $400 off — a substantial discount for this powerful device, even while current RAM and storage prices skyrocket. This is a laptop that can blaze through demanding creative workloads like editing 8K video, multitasking across several apps and iPhone integrations, all while supporting up to three external displays.

Industry observers note that the Mac Mini with the base model M6 chip is the latest, most affordable Mini in Apple’s lineup right now, and a fantastic option for anyone looking for a powerful, affordable desktop computer to use with their own peripherals. This M6 config features 16GB of unified memory, three Thunderbolt 4 ports, an HDMI port, and a 2.5Gb Ethernet port in the back, and two USB-C ports and a headphone jack in front. It also supports up to three external displays, easily anchoring your entire workspace while taking up only five inches of space.

Mac Pro  / Image: Cliff Joseph / ZDNet.

The Mac Studio is a powerful pro desktop with an M5 Max chip that enables remarkable on-device AI compute. Blast through creative projects and professional workflows with the advanced graphics architecture and faster memory and storage.

Pair the Magic Mouse with any MacBook or Mac for seamless scrolling. The mouse is rechargeable and lasts about a month between charges.

#28070. Tech Report: Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced.

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1141 w)
📖 Baca

Tech Report: Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced.

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1141 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them.
  • Sources indicate that the exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does.
  • It has been revealed that patch, Nov 21: Posts on both Hacker News and X report that OpenRouter has sent customers an email notifying them that some of their prompts may have been read.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve.

Sources indicate that the exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does. Many of today’s AI apps use services such as OpenRouter or Vercel that act as brokers. These “AI routers,” sometimes also known as “AI gateways,” receive large numbers of prompts sent from AI app end users and route them to an available inference engine based on criteria such as the one charging the lowest price or being best suited for the given task. Instead of using Anthropic, OpenAI, or another big provider, the developer hires an AI router to find the most suitable model.

It has been revealed that patch, Nov 21: Posts on both Hacker News and X report that OpenRouter has sent customers an email notifying them that some of their prompts may have been read. OpenRouter cited the research and said that it received a report that the potential exposure involved prompts sent to MiniMax, a China-based model provider. OpenRouter said the researchers’ planted URLs were accessed whether the prompts were sent to MiniMax directly or through three other resellers: AtlasCloud, Novita, and StreamLake. OpenRouter has removed a “Zero Data Retention” label from MiniMax-model endpoints. Hat tip: Sulat.com.

According to recent reports, to test for potential leakage, researcher HD Moore assembled a collection of Amazon Web Services access keys, functioning credentials tied to empty AWS accounts, passwords for services such as SSH, and unique URLs, DNS names, and private git repository references. None of the secrets had ever been used before, and he controlled the infrastructure that received any requests using the credentials. He then seeded each secret into exactly one prompt sent to a single provider. In the event any of the secrets were leaked, these “canaries”—so called because they resemble the role of that bird when taken into coal mines—would allow Moore to identify each link in the chain that was responsible.

The findings are striking. They included:.

Industry observers note that “We sent nearly two million AI prompts containing unique, trackable secrets to AI providers, then watched where those secrets surfaced,” Moore, the chief research officer of security firm Dragos, wrote Thursday. “What we found revealed security breaches, prompt theft, and widespread failures to protect customer data.”.

Although prompts are encrypted in transit, they are decrypted at each hop inside the large inference reseller network. The prompt is first sent to an AI router, which reads the plaintext in it to determine the most suitable inference providers to handle the request. Often, the prompt is then sent to a pool of available models, which sometimes run inside different hosting providers. Prompts can also pass from one AI router to another one. Each one of these players is likely to log the prompt and store it for as long as its policies call for (if not indefinitely).

Sources indicate that the most concerning finding was the breach of three separate hosting providers. The attackers who compromised one of the providers reused “a couple hundred” of the AWS keys. Moore wrote:.

Each key was sent in exactly one request to one provider, all within a few short windows in late October, and every request we sent during those windows was stolen. Some of the stolen keys came from requests that the provider rejected before a model ever ran—this tells us that the attacker was copying requests at the provider’s front door, and not somewhere deeper in the inference stack. In the other two breaches, some of the stolen requests were marked as ZDR. A privacy flag doesn’t help when the attacker is already inside.

Parties tied to the hack of these three providers then tested each key, in some cases within hours of being seeded, to see what kind of resources it gave access to. The parties looked through S3 buckets, secrets managers, and parameter stores in search of still more credentials. They also tried to enable hosted models in AWS Bedrock and added their own IAM owners to maintain access. In all, the stolen bait keys were used “tens of thousands” of times in AWS API calls.

Secrets sent to two of the hacked providers were rapidly used together, almost immediately, from the same rented server. That means the providers were almost certainly compromised by the same adversary.

Sources indicate that as noted earlier, some of the secrets were stolen by the resellers themselves. To lure prompts to their servers, they offered low prices. Then they turned on request logging and waited. Moore identified them by sending requests to the same model through different sellers. When credentials were later reused when sent through one seller and not another, the researcher knew it was the reseller, not the model provider, that was responsible.

Last, the canary experiment revealed that some providers are scraping secret URLs put into the prompts, in violation of privacy terms. Moore wrote:.

Recent findings suggest that the clearest example involves a Chinese AI lab. This lab’s systems fetched the secret URLs from more than half of the prompts that we sent to its models between July and October, including roughly two-thirds of the requests marked as “no data collection” or Zero Data Retention. The scraper typically highlighted up two or three days after the request.

It has been revealed that this wasn’t limited to requests sent to the lab directly. Several US hosting providers resell this lab’s models, and prompts sent to those providers triggered the exact same scraper—the prompts were flowing back to the lab. A customer who picked a US provider specifically to keep their data in the U.S. didn’t get what they paid for. Later on, a git client on a different cloud started trying to clone the private repositories referenced in our prompts, but only for prompts that used this lab’s models.

According to recent reports, the researcher said he found one US hosting provider crawling a secret URL more than two months after it was used in a single inference call to its search endpoint. Another ran a scraper that came back for URLs days after each request, regardless of the AI router used to reach it.

According to recent reports, the blockbuster research is the latest indictment exposing the lax privacy and security that’s endemic in much of the AI ecosystem. The findings mean that people who want to ensure secrets they put into prompts stay private face a daunting task that isn’t likely to become easier any time soon.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, you can stream GTA VI from your PS5 to a PC using PS Remote Play, then share your gameplay with friends through Discord’s screen-sharing feature. I tested this setup on launch day and found that video quality remained consistent, although input lag made driving and shooting more difficult.

In a recent development, also: Can your PC run GTA VI? The minimum requirements to expect.

I normally don’t preorder or buy games on Day One, but c’mon, it’s GTA VI. I was the first in my friend group to play on launch day; I was like a kid on Christmas morning. But I didn’t want to keep it all to myself, so I made plans to stream the game via Discord for a private watch party with my friends.

Using both the PS Remote Play app and Discord’s built-in screen sharing, I created an imperfect-but-workable solution — and got to have a bonkers good time with my friends despite GTA VI being a single-player experience.

In a recent development, the first few hours of GTA VI are absolutely Florida Man Simulator, and what better way to honor that than to find a jerry-rigged solution for sharing gameplay? The PS Remote Play app lets you stream gameplay to your smart TV or PC from your PS5 console, and then I simply used Discord’s screen-sharing feature to show the app to my friends.

I was most worried that both programs might compress the video feed into a pixelated, bitcrushed mess, but frequent check-ins from the peanut gallery assured me that everything was running smoothly and looking crisp.

It has been revealed that also: Need a GTA VI headset? Use headphones you own – with settings tweaks.

Using PS Remote Play did add a significant amount of input lag to my GTA VI gameplay, and while it’s easy enough to compensate for, it does make gunplay and driving slightly frustrating experiences.

Sources indicate that as someone who is more used to real-world driving simulators like American Truck Simulator and Assetto Corsa Competizione, the driving already feels a touch too floaty and slippery, and the lag means you have to plan every turn and stop well in advance to avoid sliding into the environment or slamming into the back of an NPC vehicle and getting the cops called on you. The gunplay lag is much easier to compensate for, especially if you keep your focus buffed and the meter filled to pull off trick shots and down multiple enemies without wasting ammo.

Streaming GTA VI to my friends also helped spark some interesting conversations about where we could see different influences from other Rockstar games, like the Heat system working very similarly to Red Dead Redemption 2’s Wanted mechanic: If you get caught committing a crime but manage to evade the police, that area of the map holds “heat,” so police and NPCs will be more vigilant and quicker to respond to reported crimes.

We also took plenty of time to just poke around Leonida and get a feel for the game world.

Also: Fake GTA 6 PC downloads are flooding the web.

Sources indicate that we went deep-sea fishing at night, searched underwater wrecks for treasures to sell, drove dirt bikes through the swamps, and watched several hours of in-game television (Right Wing on Weazel News is actually very good, and the Visit Leonida tourism ads are comedy gold). At some point, we fully abandoned the main storyline and even the side quests to go looking for Sasquatch and UFOs in the Grassrivers (the in-game equivalent of the Florida Everglades).

Industry observers note that as long as you have a decently fast internet connection, you’re likely to maintain consistent video quality while streaming GTA VI to friends on Discord or even to a live audience on YouTube or Twitch. Despite being captured by both PS Remote Play and Discord, the video feed wasn’t compressed much in my testing.

In a recent development, I don’t pay for Discord Nitro, so I streamed GTA VI in 720p — not the best video quality, but it’s good enough for a private watch party with my friends on our own server. If you do pay for Nitro, you’ll be able to stream in 1080p full HD to better show off GTA VI’s beautiful visuals (seriously, it is a breathtaking game, and I am very sad I can’t actually visit and dance with Rhonda & her pet iguana, Princess).

Also: Best early Black Friday gaming laptop deals.

You could also use a program like OBS to capture gameplay footage from your PS5 without having to set up an expensive capture card, making it that much simpler to share GTA VI with a live audience on YouTube or Twitch. And even though there is a touch of noticeable lag when streaming via PS Remote Play, it’s not bad enough to detract from the fun, even after the Day 1 excitement faded.

BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that back in October, I wrote about WordCraft, the open-source clone of MS Word. After writing that piece, I assumed that I’d go back to writing in Google Docs, but I reconsidered. Why? Privacy. I don’t want Google to dip its fingers into the well of my creativity, so I initially decided to write all of my books locally.

Sources indicate that and now that I have my own writing app (which is already available for Linux and will be available soon for both MacOS and Windows), I don’t even need a word processor for first drafts. I do, however, need it for the editing process.

Also: Someone made a free Photoshop clone – so I had to try it on Linux.

In light of my review of WordCraft, I thought I’d stick with it and see how I felt about the app after a month or so. That month has passed, and I’m still using WordCraft.

I won’t use the Windows OS, and if given the opportunity, I will always choose open-source software over proprietary software, and I have a very good reason for that. Without Windows, using MS Word is a challenge. Yes, there’s Wine, but that’s an extra layer of complication. And, of course, there’s Office365, but I want nothing to do with third-party cloud storage or services.

Sources indicate that soon after I wrote the piece about WordCraft, there was concern about it being nothing more than a vehicle for malicious code. Because the app is open-source, I was able to clone the source from its GitHub repository, add it to a new VS Code workspace, and have GitHub Copilot automatically scan the source for bugs, errors, and malicious code.

The scan came up clean. I ran it again, and again, it came up clean.

Also: I tried the free PowerPoint clone on Linux – it beats LibreOffice and Google Slides.

Recent findings suggest that after three attempts, I decided WordCraft was as safe to use as any software, so I continued using it. And although it was still in early development, I’d already found it to be more than stable enough for my needs.

According to recent reports, the other thing about using this open-source clone is that updates come faster and more frequently than MS Word. I’m not saying the updates are daily, but I have found them to be almost weekly. And with each enhancement, the software runs even better.

At this point, I find WordCraft to already be better than most word processor apps I’ve used on both Linux and MacOS.

After using WordCraft for a month, I’ve found a few important aspects (for me) that are marked improvements over other (similar) apps.

First off, WordCraft is stupid fast. No other word processor (regardless of OS) opens this swiftly. Seriously…click on the launcher and WordCraft is instantly ready to go. Given how much I write, speed is an crucial factor. The opening and closing of the app isn’t the only zippy aspect of WordCraft; the UI responds instantly, saving is immediate, and closing the app happens as fast as you can click.

Also: I tried the free Adobe Acrobat clone – and finally have a pro PDF editor on Linux.

I’ve come to appreciate its collaboration features between users who work with MS Office and me. I’ve used nearly every word processor on the market, and the only app that can top WordCraft’s collaboration with MS Office is MS Office. Whether it’s text formatting, page layout, track changes, or comments, WordCraft does it all to a T. Not having to deal with the frustration of constantly reformatting or structuring a document simply because the tool I use can’t seem to properly interpret what MS Office does is a breath of fresh air. That’s not to place the blame on other apps, but we all know that where MS Word goes, other apps must follow.

I’ve imported full book manuscripts (in .docx file format) and had zero problems. Even manuscripts with hundreds of comments and track changes didn’t cause a single glitch with WordCraft. And as far as the review tools, no other non-MS Office app can hold a candle to what WordCraft offers. In fact, it was the poorly designed review tools (track changes and comments) in LibreOffice that sent me packing from that app.

Also: Why the future of Linux is rolling – thanks to AI.

Sources indicate that wordCraft is also reliable. I’ve lost so much work to Apple Pages that I eventually deemed it absolutely off limits. This comes as a shock, given how young WordCraft is. This app has existed for about as long as I’ve been using it, and I already trust it more than other apps I’ve used. Since I adopted WordCraft, I haven’t lost a single bit of work.

It has been revealed that in my original review, I noted that there was a delay in typing in WordCraft. Although there is still a slight delay (we’re talking milliseconds), it’s much better than it was when I first used the app.

If there were two features that I could add to WordCraft, it would be user-customizable themes and Grammarly integration. Although Grammarly doesn’t have a strict ban on open-source integration, there are issues with technical UI requirements, developer tools that are deprecated, and licensing issues that cause problems with integration. Maybe, someday in the future, WordCraft will achieve that integration.

You bet. Until something better comes along (which I don’t expect), WordCraft is my default word processor. No, I will not be using WordCraft for novels (that’s where Quillwriter comes into play), but for everything else, you can bet that WordCraft will continue to be my go-to for tech writing and other non-fiction work.

BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied.

According to recent reports, while BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities. CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria.

According to recent reports, aware of an exploited vulnerability not at the moment listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form. Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.

Meta reconsiders 2030 net-zero goal amid record emissions from AI data centers

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, meta’s executives are rethinking the company’s original goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030.
  • The tech giant’s 2026 sustainability report claims that “our long-term ambitions haven’t changed, but our operating environment has,” according to an introduction from Rachel Peterson, vice president of data centers at Meta, and Blair Swedeen, global head of net zero and sustainability at Meta.
  • “We are re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones—including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets—so our approach reflects current operating realities while keeping progress transparent year over year,” Peterson and Swedeen wrote in the report.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, meta’s executives are rethinking the company’s original goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030. That revelation in Meta’s latest sustainability report comes as the company reported a record percentage increase in greenhouse gas emissions that exceeds any other Big Tech competitor racing to build fresh AI data centers.

The tech giant’s 2026 sustainability report claims that “our long-term ambitions haven’t changed, but our operating environment has,” according to an introduction from Rachel Peterson, vice president of data centers at Meta, and Blair Swedeen, global head of net zero and sustainability at Meta. In the November 19, 2026, report, they attributed the changing conditions and the need for a rethink to how “demand for AI infrastructure has grown faster than almost anyone projected.”.

“We are re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones—including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets—so our approach reflects current operating realities while keeping progress transparent year over year,” Peterson and Swedeen wrote in the report.

Meta’s statement about re-evaluating its 2030 emissions goal is a significant public acknowledgment, given that Amazon, Google, and Microsoft have all stuck by their original sustainability goals so far.

It has been revealed that but all the companies have acknowledged challenges in balancing their original sustainability goals against the breakneck buildout of hyperscale data centers. Despite efforts to invest in more renewable energy projects, Meta and its rivals are still often pushing forward on AI data centers that rely on burning natural gas to generate electricity.

Meta’s report described the company’s total emissions as surging from 15.6 million metric tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent in 2024 to more than 21.7 million metric tonnes in 2025.

According to recent reports, that would make Meta’s annual carbon footprint roughly comparable to total emissions for the state of Idaho, while surpassing the total emissions of states such as Hawaii, Maine, South Dakota, and New Hampshire. The manufacturer attributed much of this emissions increase to “capital goods,” like as data center servers.

That also represents a nearly 40 percent increase in Meta’s carbon footprint between 2024 and 2025, which is the highest percentage year-over-year increase for total emissions reported by any of the four major US tech giants.

According to recent reports, for comparison, Microsoft reported a 25 percent increase in its overall carbon footprint, Google reported an 18 percent increase, and Amazon’s report described a 16 percent increase between 2024 and 2025. However, Meta still likely has one of the smallest total carbon footprints among the Significant Tech companies.

Meta’s approach to achieving net-zero emissions has included developing fresh renewable energy projects to match emissions and using carbon removal technology.

According to recent reports, but even when factoring in such efforts, Meta still reported net emissions increasing from more than 8.1 million metric tonnes to more than 11.8 million metric tonnes for 2025. That represents a 45 percent increase.

From a water consumption standpoint, Meta reported progress in reducing facility consumption from 825 million gallons in 2024 to 790 million gallons in 2025.

Yet that positive trend is tempered by the fact that Meta also described an increase in water consumption from “areas with water stress,” rising from 198 million gallons in 2024 to 246 million gallons in 2025.

Recent findings suggest that meta also reported a sharp increase in water consumption related to purchased electricity—the amount of water consumed by related power generation—from 19 billion gallons in 2024 to more than 26 billion gallons in 2025. This once again highlights that, for data centers, the far bigger water usage comes from the power plants that supply electricity to data centers as opposed to data centers directly using water for cooling.

Sources indicate that still, some minor credit is due. The publication Data Center Dynamics pointed out that “Meta is the only hyperscaler to report indirect water use, a growing concern as data centers shift to closed-loop cooling systems that, despite using less water at source, require more electricity to run.”.

It would very much be in the public interest for other Significant Tech companies to follow suit on the reporting front—and public pressure continues to build after the AI backlash impact on US midterm election results.

Latest Update: Claude can ship code for you now – how to try it (if you dare)

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (906 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, developers are already using Claude Code and other AI-powered coding tools like OpenAI’s Codex in droves, but some still want to check code themselves before pushing it.
  • According to recent reports, with Claude Ship, revealed in beta Monday, “Claude can now review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team’s policy allows,” Anthropic mentioned.
  • Also: How I made a paid Mac app in 11 days with Claude – without writing a single line of code.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, developers are already using Claude Code and other AI-powered coding tools like OpenAI’s Codex in droves, but some still want to check code themselves before pushing it. A latest feature from Anthropic is banking on more adventurous, agent-first coders being comfortable with handing even that last step off to AI.

According to recent reports, with Claude Ship, revealed in beta Monday, “Claude can now review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team’s policy allows,” Anthropic mentioned. The feature is geared toward individual developers or companies who want to move faster or already delegate a significant amount of coding tasks to agents.

Also: How I made a paid Mac app in 11 days with Claude – without writing a single line of code.

“Teams stay in control of where it runs and which changes need a person,” Anthropic noted. “The goal: ship code as fast as teams write it.”.

The upcoming feature uses two new agents alongside Code Review, which Anthropic released in March for Teams and Enterprise plans. Code Review first collects, organizes, and posts findings to a PR. Then, Anthropic said, the agents, PR Steward and Claude Approvals, guide a PR “through review, fixes, and an approval decision so teams don’t have to manage each step manually.”.

Sources indicate that PR Steward can’t approve or merge pull requests, designed instead to participate “on failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and review feedback from Code Review, other review tools, or team members.” It also documents what it changed in each push through comments and provides instructions for how to undo it, should developers want to. Throughout the process, developers can give Claude instructions or tell it to stop by commenting @claude.

Also: I tried replacing Claude Code with a local AI stack that’s completely free – how it went.

Recent findings suggest that as a final step, Claude Approvals references whatever policy the user or team abides by (which developers provide as a repo file), and additional signals developers set, like Code Review findings, before approving changes autonomously if allowed. If not, it will seek out “deeper human sign-off,” Anthropic mentioned.

“It works like a smarter CODEOWNERS file,” the release added. Anthropic stated it recommends that most customers enable those additional checks “first in observe-only mode to build confidence before configuring branch protection to require Claude Approvals’ green light.”.

Admins can select which repos the feature runs in and adjust settings as needed.

But Claude Ship isn’t meant for everyone.

“Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now,” Anthropic remarked in the release, noting that its own Claude Code team uses Claude to write a majority of the code it needs.

ZDNET senior contributing editor David Gewirtz remarked the idea of shipping code at the speed of writing it “raises the hair on the back of my neck.” But he added that, given how impressive Claude Code has been thus far, he wouldn’t be surprised if Anthropic’s deployment tools were equally effective.

Industry observers note that also: Claude Code vs. Codex: Why I use both and how to choose one (if you must).

It has been revealed that “But, it does depend on the team’s workflow and the kind of development they’re doing,” he said. “It’s not something for every team and certainly not for every indy developer, but for certain deployment processes, it could shave a ton of time off turnaround, saving money and potentially sending fixes to customers much faster. ‘Tis cool.”.

Ultimately, Gewirtz noted he has reasons to both trust the tool and be concerned about what it means for younger developers in the workplace.

“Since that workflow is often assigned to less experienced members of the team, it’s likely that Claude would be as accurate, although it’s one more way to shut the junior members out of where they add value to the firm and grow their skills to become senior decision makers,” he said.

Recent findings suggest that developer platforms overall are adapting to the new state of the industry. Entire, a GitHub competitor started by the Microsoft-owned platform’s former CEO, is built around the expectation that developers are working side-by-side with agents.

It has been revealed that individuals with a Pro, Max, or Ultra subscription can use the /ship command now available in Claude Code, meaning “users won’t notice any significant increase in token usage,” an Anthropic representative explained. Team and Enterprise users can use Claude Ship for Github repos, and it is billed on tokens, so your overall bill may change.

Still, that depends on the number of PRs owners are putting through Claude Ship — to avoid any surprises, admins can set spending limits for both Code Review and the new PR Steward agent. They can also turn Claude Ship on for an entire repo, meaning developers won’t need the /ship command.

Industry observers note that anthropic added that certain Enterprise organizations “can claim at least $10,000 in Claude Ship credits to use within 30 days of claiming” by Jan. 15, 2027.

Also: How I safely run my OpenClaw AI agent 24/7 on a Mac – with Claude Code standing guard.

As with other Claude features, like the still-to-come Meetings, customers with a zero-data-retention policy and other privacy configurations don’t have access to Claude Ship.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google’s flagship search experience is evolving into an AI experience with stunning speed. Even time-tested elements of search are getting AI makeovers, and the latest to get this treatment is the search homepage on Google.com. A redesign that has been in testing for the past few weeks is now official, bringing easier access to AI chats and dropping the dedicated search button entirely.

Google search VP Robby Stein confirmed on X that Google is deploying the latest desktop search page after a successful test. The page will now have a few more buttons under the search bar, all connected to AI features. There’s an image-generation button, one for analyzing files, and one for brainstorming with Gemini. The “I’m Feeling Lucky” button remains, but the Google Search button that sat next to it is gone.

The search button has obviously been a part of Google’s search page forever. However, it wasn’t in a very convenient location in the modern interface. When you begin typing a query, the autocomplete suggestions cover that button. You have to click out of the text field to access the button, which is an extra step compared to simply mashing the Enter key to run your search.

The other big change brings your recent AI conversations to the forefront. If you’re logged in to Google, the search homepage will have an expandable sidebar on the left with your recent AI Mode search threads. This sidebar will also be accessible on the results page. According to Stein, the sidebar made a “big difference” in how people made progress on their web searches, calling it a “simpler way to pick up where you left off.”.

It’s easy to feel frustrated by changes like this if you don’t like Google’s fresh AI approach to search. But at the same time, the loss of functionality is minimal. Google probably has usage data that demonstrates that particular search button was rarely used. Most people probably just hit Enter or click an autocomplete suggestion to go to the results.

This change says more about Google’s priorities and the future of search. AI features get prominent buttons, and your AI conversations now have a whole sidebar UI. Meanwhile, traditional search is increasingly de-emphasized. There may come a day when AI Mode takes over completely, forcing you to manually select the old-fashioned version of search. It does feel like Google is inching in that direction.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that GTA VI isn’t yet available for PC, but that hasn’t stopped scammers from flooding the web with fake downloads that could put your PC at risk. These range from poorly made GTA VI clones vibe-coded with AI to actively malicious, virus-riddled downloads designed to turn your PC into a crypto mining operation or steal your money and data. Cybersecurity provider Kaspersky reported recording 27,416 detections of GTA VI-related malware and unwanted apps since June.

In a recent development, also: Can your PC run GTA VI? Minimum requirements to expect.

According to recent reports, you can probably spot the majority of GTA VI scams a mile away, but you’re never immune to an official-looking webpage or the promise of a free copy. No matter how official a page seems, unless the news is from Rockstar itself, you’re being lied to. And take any claims of the game code being dumped and cracked for PC with a large grain of salt. The only way you can play on PC is to use the PlayStation Remote Play app to stream from your console to your PC.

Rockstar has a history of making PC gamers wait their turn for titles. Red Dead Redemption 2 got its PC port a year after consoles, and GTA 5 came to PCs almost two years after launch. While there is a rumor that Rockstar will be bring GTA VI to PCs early next year, there hasn’t been an official announcement.

Industry observers note that so what if you got fooled into downloading a fake version of GTA VI? Fortunately, cleaning up and protecting your PC is a fairly straightforward process.

Industry observers note that alright, so you’ve downloaded a fake version of GTA VI. Your very first move should be to immediately uninstall the program. Getting rid of the software limits a scammer’s or hacker’s options for hijacking your PC. But you can’t stop there.

Recent findings suggest that the fake GTA VI program itself might be gone now, but it could still be hiding malicious files deep inside your PC and wreaking havoc. Running antivirus software like AVG Avast, even the free version, can help track them all down for quarantine and destruction.

Also: I streamed GTA VI to my PC – it was awesome, even with lag.

Check out our tested picks for the best antivirus protection here.

A “cracked” PC program is any software whose copy protection has been circumvented and removed, while a keygen is a program that reverse-engineers the license validation algorithm your PC uses to generate fake but official-looking product keys.

Also: Need a GTA VI headset? Use headphones you own – with tweaks.

Both processes are heavily involved in the software pirating and sharing community, and you’ll be able to find hundreds of customers across dozens of less-than-legal forums claiming to have dumped the source code for GTA VI and cracked it, making it available for PC users and modders.

While a few might actually be trying to distribute the game for free, no strings attached, most will likely have a host of malware hiding inside to hijack your PC.

Recent findings suggest that as my grandfather used to say: If it smells like b.s., it is. The vast majority of GTA VI download scams fall apart under the slightest bit of scrutiny, so don’t be afraid to follow the money, as it were.

It has been revealed that notorious cracker/leaker Cyberleek claimed to have the entire source code for the Xbox build of GTA VI and would release it on Nov. 23 — but only if his scammy crypto coin hit $15 million in market cap — which was then lowered to $6 million in a spectacular failure of self-negotiation. The hacker, or group of hackers, did post a collection of dumped assets from the game online (character models, texture packs, etc.), but there was no executable file needed to run the program.

Also: How to play GTA VI on your PC today – with a free app.

Today, in a post I won’t be linking for legal reasons, Cyberleek has seemingly made good on their promise and updated their file dump with an executable. But it remains to be seen if the .exe is authentically decompiled so that modders and emulation developers can use it or if it’s another bluff in a long line of overpromises and lackluster deliveries. Either way, what Cyberleek is doing is highly illegal, and I cannot advise you strongly enough not to touch this download.

Even if it is a way to run GTA VI on your PC without a workaround or an official port, it’s also likely hiding all kinds of malicious code that will allow Cyberleek to hijack your PC and turn it into a covert crypto miner to boost their meme coin value before disappearing into the ether like usual. But if you’re gullible enough to fall for this very obvious scam from one of the most infamous online scammers, chalk it up as a hard lesson you needed to learn.
